steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Julius Caesar raided Britain in 55 and 54 BCE but did not establish permanent occupation

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Emperor Claudius invaded Britain in 43 CE to gain military prestige and legitimise his reign

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Caractacus led British resistance but was defeated and taken to Rome in chains

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Boudica of the Iceni led a major revolt in 60-61 CE after Roman brutality towards her family

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why did Claudius invade Britain in 43 CE? | Q: What caused Boudica's revolt? | Q: How far did Romanisation change British culture?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Claudius needed a military victory to legitimise his position as emperor. Conquering Britain, which Caesar had only raided, would give him prestige and secure his political authority. | After her husband died, Romans seized Iceni lands, flogged Boudica and assaulted her daughters. This brutality combined with heavy taxation triggered widespread rebellion. | Significantly in the south and east with towns, villas, baths and roads transforming daily life. But in the north and west Celtic culture persisted. Romanisation was uneven across Britain.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Discuss both resistance AND cooperation — not all Britons fought Rome Boudica is the key individual — know her story in detail Hadrian's Wall is a physical symbol of empire and frontier policy Use archaeological evidence alongside literary sources Romanisation is the key concept — explain what it meant in practice
